description: The true path of the miniature: part of the story is a statement by a narrator who is not to be believed in everything. One thing he says is against what the other narrator knows himself; that one statement is set aside, and another of his own is kept and turned on him.

moves.why: Finch was locked up at Cross Street from ten until seven, on the Inspector's own key: Kemp did not see him at the window.
Finch could not have been at the bank.

moves.see: it was done with the keys
moves.why: Both doors were opened with their keys.

moves.see: the keys never left Kemp's belt
moves.why: And Kemp says himself that the keys never left his belt.
The man with the keys, who put the blame on a man who could not have been there.
